name: Prescribed Sections in Complements of Obstructions
statement: Let $S$ be an irredundantly embedded ample forbidden pc-minor with three resolving one-concept additions $a_0,a_+,a_-$ having pairwise distinct acquired supports. For nonempty proper $K\in\mathcal D_{\rm amp}$ on a disjoint coordinate set $D$ and $u\in Q_D$, set $X_K=(S\times Q_D)\cup(\{a_0\}\times K)\cup(\{a_+\}\times(Q_D\setminus\{u\}))\cup(\{a_-\}\times(Q_D\setminus\{\bar u\}))$. Then $X_K$ is an ample forbidden pc-minor, and the section of its cube complement at old word $a_0$ is exactly $Q_D\setminus K$. If this complementary section is nonpeelable, both $X_K$ and its cube complement are nonpeelable and $X_K$ cannot be obtained from its ambient cube by corner deletions. Moreover $|X_K|=(|S|+2)2^{|D|}+|K|-2$.
proof: The three occurrence rows are nonempty, proper, ample, and peelable. The two punctured cubes own opposite full facets for every coordinate of $D$, so the common-seed occurrence-cover theorem makes $X_K$ an ample forbidden pc-minor. Only the row $K$ occurs at old word $a_0$, giving the asserted complementary section. This is a proper pc-minor of the complement because the complement also contains $(a_+,u)$. A peeling of the complement would induce an ample-prefix order on the section, so a nonpeelable section forces the whole complement to be nonpeelable. The ambient-cube descent criterion then excludes a descent to $X_K$. The four parts are disjoint, and direct counting yields the order formula.
comments: The theorem prescribes an arbitrary complement section arising as the complement of a nonempty proper dismantlable ample row; it does not claim that the resulting obstruction is terminal under obstruction-preserving corner deletion.
